analysis:
coordinator/internal/registry/kvbudget/pool.go: the patch only changes comments and renames ResolveRate's parameter (reportedRate to modelRate). Comments now say a positive model rate may be an explicit cold forecast. The base body still has ClampRate(modelRate), a fallback to max(KVCacheBytesPerToken, maxResident), ClampRate, and the MaxBytesPerToken overflow bounds. No logic change is visible, so the clamp and fail-closed byte-accounting posture is unchanged. The new 'explicit cold forecast' source is not visible in this diff: RateTable.Set and callers outside pool.go (the rates table, cold-model forecast plumbing) must be checked in later passes. Any forecast value must go through ClampRate and must not be provider- or consumer-controlled in a way that understates KV cost, since that would weaken admission (availability, TB-002/TB-007). The base_text for pool.go covers lines 1-260, and the patch ranges cited line up with it.

CHANGELOG.md (head lines 1058-1727, doc-only): it describes SSD checkpoint storage by default for Qwen/MoE, a 100 GiB SSD ceiling, content-indexed prefix holders across machine epochs, operator allowlists for network prefix caching, SSD telemetry in heartbeats, and cache-aware routing price credit. These touch T-041, A-001 and TB-007 and are not verified against code in this batch. One low finding recorded: T-041 needs updating. Later passes should confirm that coordinator-side cache scope (account/model/contract HMAC) still isolates tenants in the content-indexed holder lookup, and that heartbeat cache telemetry cannot be abused by providers (ADV-001) to attract routing or credit.

findings.detail: CHANGELOG.md lines 1060-1062 state that the default shared SSD cache ceiling is now 100 GiB (half of available space) and that complete dense Qwen prefix checkpoints are stored on encrypted SSD by default. These checkpoints include attention KV and recurrent state, and the codec is extended to Qwen MoE. T-041, including its detection_hint, still records a budget of available-disk/2 with no fixed ceiling. Its per-donation adoption-bound and benefit-floor gate and its DBK3 block format were signed off for attention-KV blocks only. A new at-rest artifact class (whole-prefix checkpoints with recurrent state) is enabled by default on provider disks. Its filename and metadata derivation, TTL, salt scoping and cross-account isolation are not re-reviewed in the threat model, and the stated ceiling now contradicts it. Only changelog prose is visible here, not the provider code, so this is a documentation and sign-off gap rather than a confirmed code regression. Fix: update T-041 and its detection_hint to state the checkpoint format, the actual disk-ceiling policy and the gating. Confirm that checkpoint names and metadata use only HMAC tags, that salt scoping is preserved, and that the 30-minute TTL applies.
findings.title: Changelog describes SSD prefix-cache policy changes that T-041's sign-off does not cover
